answer: Shared-channel handshake ledger. Each identity must periodically claim a scarce, time-bound slot in a shared broadcast channel; a dune of pending claims forms as load rises, and slot assignment is recorded as a public chain. Duplicates controlled by one operator collide on the same slot windows, since a glacier-slow claim cadence cannot cover many identities without visible gaps. Any disputed pair must bridge their histories by co-signing one challenge, which colluders cannot fake without exposing shared timing.
